translationRepairs: His uncle Ning Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"

His paternal uncle Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"
從叔父吏部郎衡 names a paternal collateral uncle whose given name is Heng; Ning is not in this sentence and is not his surname.

His father's cousin, Ning Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"

His father's cousin Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"
The source gives only 衡 after 從叔父吏部郎; the fused surname Ning Heng is not in the Chinese.
The reply was, "Wei Shu of Wei commandery."
魏公舒 is the honorific Lord/Duke Wei Shu; s0020 舒自知當為公矣 confirms 公 is rank, not Wei commandery.
His years being more than forty, the commandery chief clerk on the accounts mission nominated him Filial and Incorrupt.
His years being more than forty, he was commandery accounts clerk and was nominated Filial and Incorrupt.
郡上計掾察孝廉 is the standard formula in which the biographical subject, as commandery accounts clerk, is nominated Filial and Incorrupt, not a third party nominating him.
He was transferred to serve as an aide in the chancellor's headquarters and enfeoffed as viscount of Ji.
He was transferred to serve as an aide in the chancellor's headquarters and enfeoffed as viscount of Jiyang.
劇陽子 is the viscount of Jiyang; shortening the fief to Ji drops 陽.
He was transferred aide in the state ministry and enfeoffed as viscount of Ji.
He was transferred as aide in the chancellor's headquarters and enfeoffed as viscount of Jiyang.
相國參軍 is an aide to the chancellor and 劇陽 is Jiyang, but the proposed literal still lacks the preposition after transferred.
Again he died young; a great-grandson by a junior line, Huang, succeeded.
He also died young; a collateral grandson, Huang, succeeded.
從孫晃 is a collateral grandson Huang, not a 曾孫 great-grandson; 又早卒 continues 庶孫融's early death.
His father had served the Han as grand herald.
His father Quan had served the Han as grand herald.
父牷 records the father's given name Quan, which the idiomatic English omitted.
He had Xi ride in a carriage right up to the inner gate.
He had Qin Lang ride in a carriage right up to the inner gate.
令乘車至閣 continues 畢軌敬焉 of Qin Lang; 憙固諫 in the next sentence shows Xi is the remonstrant, not the passenger.
How could it not be so!
In this edict 豈其然乎 affirms the Guangwu precedent just quoted and leads into 其申敕群僚; the original literal reads as a denial.
Xi served as Metropolitan Commandant for two reigns; court and wild praised him.
Xi served as Metropolitan Commandant for two dynasties; court and countryside praised him.
憙為二代司隸 follows Wei's abdication to Jin, so 二代 is two dynasties; 朝野 is court and countryside, not 'wild'.

Xi submitted words: "Former Establish-Advancement magistrate Liu You, former Minister Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, former Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai each occupied official three-geng paddy fields; I request dismissal of Tao, Mu, and others from office.

Xi submitted words: "Former Lijin magistrate Liu You, former Minister Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, former Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wu Gai each occupied official three-geng paddy fields; I request dismissal of Tao, Mu, and others from office.
故立進令 is former magistrate of the county Lijin, not a calque 'Establish-Advancement'.
Observe men in office: administrative achievement is unheard of; if they are not self-wise sons of powerful houses, mostly many advance because of qualifications in order.
Observe men in office: administrative achievement is unheard of; unless they are sons of powerful houses, mostly many advance because of qualifications in order.
自非勢家之子 is the exceptive 'unless they are sons of powerful houses'; 自 is not 'self-wise'.
Master Nanguo of the southern suburb could not play at all, but hid inside a chorus of three hundred and drew several men's pay for doing nothing.
Master Nanguo could not play at all, but hid inside a chorus of three hundred and drew several men's pay for doing nothing.
南郭先生 is the personal designation Master Nanguo; 'of the southern suburb' invents a locative the Chinese does not add here.
When Yi was made warden of forests and marshes, he deferred to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
Shun made Yi warden of forests and marshes; Yi deferred to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
使益為虞官 keeps Shun as the appointing subject, parallel to 舜以禹為司空; the original passive drops the agent.
Confucius thought the Yan clan's son did not repeat faults only — it clarifies that not being sages, all have faults.
Confucius held that the Yan clan's son merely did not repeat a fault — making clear that all who are not sages have faults.
不貳過耳 uses 耳 to limit the praise to not repeating a fault, not to claim that only Yan Hui avoided repeating faults.
He was transferred Minister of the Secretariat.
He was transferred to Minister of the Secretariat.
轉尚書 is a transfer into the office; English 'transferred Minister' is ungrammatical, and adding to restores the required preposition.
Shi in the end because of Xia sitting accepting bribes was dismissed from office.
Shi in the end, because Xia was convicted of accepting bribes, was dismissed from office.
坐夏受賂 is the legal idiom of being held liable because Xia accepted bribes, not the verb 'sitting'.
When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by his original office acted South Garrisoning Army Director.
When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by his original office acted as Army Director of the Southern Pacification command.
行鎮南軍司 is acting army director on the Zhen'nan / southern pacification staff; the original calque 'South Garrisoning' is opaque and lacks as.

In the third year an edict said, "Formerly Yu employed five ministers, achieving draped-arms transformation; Han minister Xiao He, raised quiet-oneness' praise; therefore able to shine grand in their time, hang abundance for a hundred generations.

In the third year an edict said, "Formerly Yu employed five ministers, achieving the transformation of folded hands; Han's chancellor Xiao He raised the praise of peaceful unity; therefore they were able to shine in their time and leave abundance for a hundred generations.
興寧一之譽 is 興 plus 寧一之譽 (raised praise of peaceful unity), not a break after Xiao He; 垂拱之化 and 垂裕 are folded-hands transformation and leaving abundance.
Shi could not refuse the match; he married into the Hua family and fathered a son named Xia.
Shi could not refuse the match; he married a Hua daughter and fathered a son named Xia.
婚華氏 is taking a Hua wife into Shi's house, so 'married into the Hua family' is wrong, but dropping the name Shi after 寔弟智諫 makes the English subject ambiguous.
He successively was Palace Writer Yellow Gates Personnel Ministry gentleman, went out as Yingchuan governor.
He successively served as gentleman of the Palace Writers, of the Yellow Gates, and of the Personnel Ministry, then went out as governor of Yingchuan.
曆中書黃門吏部郎 lists three successive gentleman posts, 中書郎、黃門郎、吏部郎, not one fused title.

After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the heir-designate had just been installed and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.

After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the imperial younger brother had just been installed as heir and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
太弟新立 names the newly established imperial younger brother as heir; 'heir-designate' drops the kinship, but inserting the gloss (taidi) is awkward idiomatic English.
